relay_restriction_policy.title: Relay Restriction Policy
relay_restriction_policy.description: Defines which senders and destinations the MTA will relay email for. 'open' means no restrictions, 'authenticated_only' requires SMTP AUTH, 'restricted' limits by IP/domain allowlist.

smtp_auth_required.title: SMTP Authentication Required for Relay
smtp_auth_required.description: Whether the MTA enforces SMTP AUTH (e.g., SASL) before permitting relay of outbound messages from non-local sources.

open_relay_test_result.title: Open Relay Test Passed (Relay Accepted Without Auth)
open_relay_test_result.description: Result of an active relay test: true if the server accepted a message from an unauthenticated external source addressed to an external destination, confirming open relay behavior.

smtp_auth_enabled.title: SMTP AUTH Enabled
smtp_auth_enabled.description: Whether SMTP AUTH (RFC 4954) is enabled and required for relay or submission on the MTA.

permitted_auth_mechanisms.title: Permitted SMTP AUTH Mechanisms
permitted_auth_mechanisms.description: List of SMTP AUTH mechanisms advertised or permitted by the MTA (e.g., PLAIN, LOGIN, CRAM-MD5, DIGEST-MD5, GSSAPI, XOAUTH2).

tls_required_before_auth.title: TLS Required Before AUTH
tls_required_before_auth.description: Whether the MTA enforces TLS (STARTTLS or implicit TLS) before permitting SMTP AUTH advertisement or exchange, preventing cleartext credential transmission.

starttls_enforcement.title: STARTTLS Enforcement Mode
starttls_enforcement.description: Whether STARTTLS is required, opportunistic (optional), or disabled for inbound and outbound SMTP connections.

tls_wrapper_mode_enabled.title: TLS Wrapper Mode (SMTPS) Enabled
tls_wrapper_mode_enabled.description: Whether the MTA listens on port 465 (SMTPS) with implicit TLS, providing an alternative fully encrypted path even when STARTTLS is not enforced on port 25/587.

plaintext_auth_permitted_without_tls.title: Plaintext Authentication Permitted Without TLS
plaintext_auth_permitted_without_tls.description: Whether the MTA allows AUTH LOGIN, AUTH PLAIN, or other cleartext authentication mechanisms over unencrypted connections, exposing credentials to interception.

minimum_tls_version.title: Minimum TLS Version
minimum_tls_version.description: The minimum TLS protocol version accepted by the MTA for inbound and outbound connections (e.g., in Postfix: smtpd_tls_protocols / smtp_tls_protocols).

weak_cipher_suites_enabled.title: Weak Cipher Suites Enabled
weak_cipher_suites_enabled.description: Indicates whether the MTA cipher suite configuration permits weak or deprecated ciphers (e.g., RC4, DES, 3DES, NULL, EXPORT, MD5-based, or anonymous DH ciphers).

tls_security_level.title: TLS Security Level
tls_security_level.description: The TLS enforcement level configured for SMTP sessions, determining whether TLS is required, opportunistic, or disabled.

inbound_spf_validation_enabled.title: Inbound SPF Validation Enabled
inbound_spf_validation_enabled.description: Whether the MTA checks SPF records on inbound mail to verify the sending IP is authorized for the sender domain.

inbound_dkim_verification_enabled.title: Inbound DKIM Signature Verification Enabled
inbound_dkim_verification_enabled.description: Whether the MTA verifies DKIM signatures on inbound messages to authenticate message integrity and sender identity.

dmarc_policy_enforcement_mode.title: DMARC Policy Enforcement Mode
dmarc_policy_enforcement_mode.description: The DMARC policy action applied by the MTA when inbound messages fail DMARC alignment checks (none, quarantine, or reject).

outbound_dkim_signing_enabled.title: Outbound DKIM Signing Enabled
outbound_dkim_signing_enabled.description: Whether the MTA cryptographically signs outbound messages with DKIM to establish sender authenticity and protect delivery reputation.

per_ip_connection_rate_limit_configured.title: Per-IP Connection Rate Limit Configured
per_ip_connection_rate_limit_configured.description: Whether the MTA enforces a maximum number of inbound connections per source IP address within a time window (e.g., Postfix smtpd_client_connection_rate_limit, Sendmail connection throttling).

max_messages_per_connection_configured.title: Max Messages Per Connection Configured
max_messages_per_connection_configured.description: Whether the MTA limits the number of messages (MAIL FROM commands) accepted per SMTP connection, preventing queue flooding via a single long-lived connection.

concurrent_connection_limit_configured.title: Concurrent Connection Limit Configured
concurrent_connection_limit_configured.description: Whether the MTA enforces a maximum number of simultaneous inbound SMTP connections (globally and/or per source IP) to prevent connection exhaustion.

auth_failure_rate_limit_configured.title: Authentication Failure Rate Limit Configured
auth_failure_rate_limit_configured.description: Whether the MTA or an upstream policy daemon limits or blocks source IPs after repeated SMTP authentication failures, mitigating brute-force credential attacks.

mta_process_run_user.title: MTA Process Runtime User
mta_process_run_user.description: The OS username under which the MTA daemon process runs (e.g., postfix, sendmail, root, mail).

mta_process_run_uid.title: MTA Process Runtime UID
mta_process_run_uid.description: The numeric UID of the OS account under which the MTA daemon runs. UID 0 indicates root.

mta_dedicated_service_account_configured.title: Dedicated Least-Privilege Service Account Configured
mta_dedicated_service_account_configured.description: Whether the MTA is configured to use a dedicated, non-privileged, non-system-shared service account with no login shell and restricted home directory.

mta_version.title: MTA Software Version
mta_version.description: The installed version string of the MTA software.

version_has_known_cve.title: Version Has Known CVE
version_has_known_cve.description: Whether the installed MTA version has at least one publicly disclosed CVE with a severity of medium or higher (CVSS >= 4.0).

days_since_last_update.title: Days Since Last MTA Update
days_since_last_update.description: Number of days elapsed since the MTA software package was last updated on the host.

credentials_stored_in_cleartext.title: Credentials Stored in Cleartext
credentials_stored_in_cleartext.description: Indicates whether SMTP relay credentials, API keys, or TLS private keys appear in cleartext within MTA configuration files (e.g., Postfix main.cf/sasl_passwd, Sendmail, Exim configuration).

config_file_permissions.title: Configuration File Permissions
config_file_permissions.description: The filesystem permission level of the MTA configuration files containing credentials, indicating whether they are world-readable, group-readable, or properly restricted to root/mail daemon only.

logged_fields.title: MTA Logged Fields
logged_fields.description: List of fields captured per message in MTA logs. Required fields for forensic completeness are: sender, recipient, message_id, source_ip, auth_outcome.

log_level_configured.title: Per-Message Log Level Configured
log_level_configured.description: Whether the MTA is configured to log at a verbosity level sufficient to capture individual message transaction details (as opposed to errors-only or disabled logging).

admin_interface_network_restriction.title: Admin Interface Network Restriction
admin_interface_network_restriction.description: Whether the administrative interface is restricted to specific trusted networks via IP allowlisting, firewall rules, or VPN requirement.

admin_interface_exposed.title: Admin Interface Network Exposed
admin_interface_exposed.description: Whether the administrative interface (e.g., Postfix admin web console, postsuper socket, or management API) is bound to a publicly routable or untrusted network interface.

admin_interface_authentication.title: Admin Interface Authentication Mechanism
admin_interface_authentication.description: The authentication mechanism enforced on the administrative interface before allowing access to management functions.

mta_sts_policy_configured.title: MTA-STS Policy Configured
mta_sts_policy_configured.description: Indicates whether a valid MTA-STS policy is published for the domain (both DNS TXT record and HTTPS policy file at /.well-known/mta-sts.txt are present and valid).

dane_tlsa_records_configured.title: DANE TLSA Records Configured
dane_tlsa_records_configured.description: Indicates whether DANE TLSA DNS records are published for the MX host(s) of the domain and the zone is DNSSEC-signed, enabling certificate validation without a CA.

attachment_type_filtering_enabled.title: Attachment Type Filtering Enabled
attachment_type_filtering_enabled.description: Whether the MTA enforces a policy to block or quarantine dangerous attachment types (e.g., .exe, .js, .vbs, .bat, macros in Office files).

mime_structure_validation_enabled.title: MIME Structure Validation Enabled
mime_structure_validation_enabled.description: Whether the MTA or an integrated filter validates MIME structure for malformed or obfuscated payloads designed to bypass scanning.

antimalware_scan_integration.title: Anti-Malware Scan Integration
antimalware_scan_integration.description: Level of anti-malware scanning integrated at the MTA layer for email attachments.

ptr_validation_enabled.title: PTR Record Validation Enabled
ptr_validation_enabled.description: Whether the MTA performs reverse DNS (PTR) lookup validation on connecting client IPs before accepting mail.

no_ptr_rejection_policy.title: No PTR Record Rejection Policy
no_ptr_rejection_policy.description: Action taken when a connecting IP has no matching PTR record: whether connections are rejected, flagged/tagged, or accepted silently.

queue_directory_world_writable.title: Mail Queue Directory World-Writable
queue_directory_world_writable.description: Indicates whether the mail spool/queue directory (e.g., /var/spool/mqueue, /var/spool/postfix) has world-write permissions (mode includes o+w), allowing any local user to write to it.

queue_directory_owner.title: Mail Queue Directory Owner
queue_directory_owner.description: The OS user that owns the mail queue/spool directory. Should be the MTA service account (e.g., postfix, mail, smmsp, mailnull). If owned by root or a non-MTA user with broad group membership, combined with loose permissions, injection risk increases.

queue_directory_group_writable_by_non_mt.title: Queue Directory Group-Writable by Non-MTA Group
queue_directory_group_writable_by_non_mt.description: Indicates whether the mail queue directory has group-write permission AND the owning group includes members beyond the MTA service account (i.e., non-MTA local users can write via group membership).
